title: boxcar control protocol v1
description: One line of the control socket: the server's Hello, a client's Request, the server's Response, or an event (StateEvent, PtyDetached, AuditEvent, AuditLagged). Each op's parameters and result are defined beside them; see docs/control-protocol.md.

AuditEvent_for_Record.description:
`{"v":1,"event":"audit","sub":K,"rec":{...}}`: a record of the subscription `sub`, `rec` the record as the log holds it. `R` is [`Record`], or a reference to one to send it without a copy. Never over [`MAX_LINE`]: a record is at most [`MAX_RECORD_BYTES`].

[`MAX_RECORD_BYTES`]: crate::limits::MAX_RECORD_BYTES

AuditLagged.description: `{"v":1,"event":"audit.lagged","sub":K,"resume_seq":R}`: the subscription `sub` fell too far behind for the server to hold its live records, and was dropped from the live stream. The records from `resume_seq` on follow, read back from the log and then live again; those before it were delivered, so nothing is missed.

failed.description: Whether the writer has failed, which stops the VM.

next_seq.description: The sequence number the writer gives the next record it writes.

AuditSubscribeParams.description: The parameters of `audit.subscribe`: `{"from_seq":S,"types":["net."], "pid":P}`, each optional. The response is [`AuditSubscribed`]; then the connection hears [`AuditEvent`]s, and [`AuditLagged`] when it falls behind, until it closes.

from_seq.description: The first seq wanted: the records from it on, those in the log and then the live ones. 1 when absent; 0 is the same. A seq beyond the log's end waits for the live records from it on.

min_score.description: Only records whose `data.score` is at least this (findings carry one; a record without a score passes). 0 to 100.

pid.description: Only the records attributed to this guest process (`subject.pid`).

types.description: Record types, each a prefix (`"net."`, or a whole type such as `"fs.write"`). Absent or empty takes every type.

next_seq.description: The seq the log's next record had when the subscription began: the records below it come from the log, the ones from it on are live.

sub.description: The subscription's id on this connection, counting from 1: the `sub` of its events. A client that does not hold several can ignore it. 0 when a server did not say.

ErrorCode.description: The error codes, exactly these; on the wire in snake_case.

oneOf.description: The line is too long, not UTF-8, not a JSON object, lacks `v`, `id` or `op`, or has parameters that do not fit the op.
`v` is not [`VERSION`].
The server has no such op.
The op cannot be done in the VM's current state.
What the op names does not exist.
The server cannot take the op now.
The connection sent more than its budget of requests; the request was dropped.
The server failed.

GuestStatus.description: What the guest's init has reported. The default is nothing yet.

exit.description: How the session ended, once it did.

init_ready.description: Whether init has said hello over the guest control channel.

session_pid.description: The session's process id in the guest, once it started.

Hash.description: A blake3 digest: `b3:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

Hello.description: The server's first line on every connection it accepts.

capabilities.description: The op families the server serves beyond `status` and `stop`, such as `pty`, `audit` and `policy.net`.

NetPolicy.description: The network policy as `policy.get` reports it and `policy.update` takes it: `{"default":"deny","allow":["example.com:443"],"deny":["10.0.0.0/8"]}`. Each rule is a target as `boxcar run --allow` takes it: `name[:port]`, `*.name[:port]`, `address[:port]` or `address/prefix[:port]`. The policy in force puts every deny before every allow, in the order given, as `boxcar run` orders `--deny` and `--allow`: the first rule that matches decides, so a deny wins over an allow of the same target. A policy file whose allows and denies are interleaved reads back from `policy.get` in this shape, which is the same policy only when no allow before a deny matches what the deny does.

allow.description: The allow rules, as targets, in order.

default.description: The verdict when no rule matches: `allow` or `deny`.

deny.description: The deny rules, as targets, in order.

PolicyUpdateParams.description: The parameters of `policy.update`: `{"net":{...},"vsock":{...}}`, each optional and each replacing its whole policy when given. The response is [`PolicyUpdated`]; the server records `policy.changed`. A rule that does not parse is a `bad_request` naming it, and nothing changes.

PolicyUpdated.description: The result of `policy.update`: `{"policy_version":N}`, the version of the policy now in force.

PolicyView.description: The result of `policy.get`: `{"net":{...},"vsock":{...},"version":N}`, the policy in force and its version (1 for the one the VM started with, one more for each `policy.update`).

version.description: 0 when a server did not say.

PtyAttachParams.description: The parameters of `pty.attach`: `{"session":"main","mode":"rw"|"ro", "replay_bytes":N}`. The response is [`PtyAttached`], after which the connection is the terminal's bytes, both ways (see [`PtyMode`]), and only those; `replay_bytes` (0 when absent) of the terminal's latest output come first, at most the server's scrollback.

PtyAttached.description: The result of `pty.attach`: `{"raw":true,"attach_id":"<hex>"}`. The attach's id (128 random bits, in hex) is what another connection watches it by ([`PtyWatchParams`]).

raw.description: `true`: the connection is raw from the next byte.

PtyDetached.description: `{"v":1,"event":"pty.detached","attach_id":"<hex>","reason":"slow"}`: the server detached the attach `attach_id` from the session's terminal. It goes to the connections that watch the attach (`pty.watch`), never into the attached connection itself, which carries only the terminal's bytes: that one just ends, after its last byte. `slow`: the client left more of the terminal's output unread than the server keeps for it, or took none for 30 s.

PtyMode.description: How a client attaches to the session's terminal.

oneOf.description: Read and write: what the client sends is typed into the session.
Read only: what the client sends is discarded.

PtyResizeParams.description: The parameters of `pty.resize`: `{"session":"main","rows":R,"cols":C}`, each of `rows` and `cols` from 1 to 65535. The response is `{}`.

PtyWatchParams.description: The parameters of `pty.watch`: `{"attach_id":"<hex>"}` (with `"session":"main"`, optionally). The response is `{}`; from then on the connection that sent it hears the attach's [`PtyDetached`].

Ready.description: The one line `boxcar run --ready-fd N` writes to fd N once the control socket is bound: `{"ready":true,"control":"<path>","session_id":"<id>"}`.

Record.description:
One audit record: one line of a session's log.

The JSON field names are these field names, except that `kind` is `type`. Unset optional fields are left out of the JSON, never written as `null`.

data.description: The payload. Its shape is decided by `kind`; see [`Payload`] for the kinds this crate defines.

prev.description: The `hash` of the previous record, or `genesis_prev` for the first.

seq.description: The record's position in the session, counting from 1 with no gaps. Only the log writer assigns it.

subject.description: The guest process the event is attributed to.

ts_guest_ns.description: The guest's own clock, for events reported from inside the guest. It orders ring 1 events among themselves.

ts_host_ns.description: Host wall-clock time (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, taken when the writer received the event. This is the only timestamp that joins events across rings.

ts_mono_ns.description: Host `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` in nanoseconds, taken at the same moment.

type.description: The dotted event type, such as `fs.open`.

id.description: Chosen by the client; the response carries it back.

Response.description: The answer to one request: `{"v":1,"id":N,"ok":true,"result":{...}}` or `{"v":1,"id":N,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}`.

id.description: The request's `id`, or 0 when the request had none that could be read, or was a long line dropped unread for being over the rate limit.

Ring.description: Which side of the VM boundary made the record: 0 the host, 1 the guest.

oneOf.description: The VM runs no sensor: it has no vsock device, or was started with `--no-sensor`.
A sensor is expected and has not reported its status yet.
The sensor attached every program and heartbeats.
The sensor runs with programs missing; `proc.sensor_status` says which.
The sensor's stream ended, or no heartbeat came for 3 s.

SensorStatus.description: The guest's sensor (ring 1), as the VMM sees its stream on vsock port 1026. The default is a VM that runs no sensor.

last_heartbeat_ns.description: Host `CLOCK_REALTIME`, in nanoseconds, when the last heartbeat arrived.

SessionId.description: A session id: a UUIDv7 in lowercase hyphenated text.

SessionOutcome.description: How the guest's session ended, as its init reported it: the exit code of the session's process, or the signal that killed it.

code.description: The exit code, when the process exited.

signal.description: The signal number, when a signal killed the process.

Source.description: The component that produced a record. On the wire, the lowercase name.

oneOf.description: The guest's session, as its init reports it over the control channel.
The session's policy, as the control socket changes it.

SpanRef.description: Where an event sits in a trace.

devices.description: The virtio devices present, by slot name in slot order, such as `fs:root` and `fs:workspace`.

sensor.description: The guest's sensor, ring 1. A server from before it reports none.

uptime_ms.description: Milliseconds since the VM was built.

oneOf.description: Ask the guest to end its session first.
Stop the vCPUs at once.

timeout_ms.description: How long a graceful stop waits for the guest; [`DEFAULT_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS`] when absent.

Subject.description: The guest identity an event is attributed to.

VmState.description: Where the VM is in its life.

oneOf.description: Built; the vCPUs have not started.
The vCPUs run.
A stop trigger fired; the stop sequence runs.
The stop sequence has run.

VsockPolicy.description: The vsock policy as `policy.get` reports it and `policy.update` takes it: `{"allow_ports":[5000]}`, the host ports a guest connection may reach besides the internal ones (`boxcar run --vsock-allow`).
